name: Plymouth Gawater
description: Plymouth Gawater is a gnome artificer and ally of the party with extensive knowledge of the Great Eldarin Tree, the Navi, the keystones, and the Mother's Prayer. He understands the significance of the prophecy and is able to identify individuals connected to the Great Tree, including Gerk. He serves as a knowledgeable guide concerning the history and purpose of the keystones and the role of the Doorman, helping the party understand their responsibilities as the new keepers. He has experience communicating with other children of the Great Tree and appears capable of recognizing unusual magical phenomena, including the mysterious white-flower girl.

log.summary: Plymouth Gawater recognized the significance of Sylan’s journal and Gerk’s connection to the Mother’s Prayer, examining Gerk and confirming him as the child of the Great Tree described by the prophecy. He explained the history connecting the Eldarin Tree, the Navi, the keystones, and the Mother’s Prayer, including that the keystones were created by distilling knowledge from the Tree’s rings and unintentionally set the Prayer in motion. Plymouth revealed that he had previously communicated with three other children of the Great Tree and that none had taken the role for roughly 1,500 years. He explained Gerk’s voluntary role as the **Doorman**, who can open, close, connect with, and protect an Arch, and oversaw the assignment of the keystones to the party. He also explained that the new keepers were expected to actively protect and use the keystones rather than merely hide them. Plymouth could see the mysterious white-flower girl and was visibly startled when Gerk successfully opened his first reality-bending doorway. He also offered Dana a bottle when she requested alcohol and discussed possible destinations accessible through the portals.
notes: Recognizes the significance of Sylan's journal and Gerk's connection to the Mother's Prayer.
Examines Gerk and confirms him as a child of the Great Tree and the individual described by the prophecy.
Has previously communicated with three other sons or daughters of the Great Tree; one accepted the challenge while two did not.
Says no son or daughter of the Mother's Prayer had come forward to take up the role for approximately 1,500 years.
Explains that accepting the role is voluntary and could benefit Gerk and all of Atlas.
Explains that Gerk's companions can become metaphorical brothers and sisters of the chosen child.
Explains the relationship between Gerk, the Eldarin Tree, the Navi, the keystones, and the Mother's Prayer.
Offers Gerk the title of Doorman and explains that the Doorman can open, close, connect with, and protect an Arch.
Explains that the keystones were created by distilling knowledge from the rings of the Eldarin Tree.
Explains that creation of the keystones unintentionally initiated the Mother's Prayer.
Explains that previous keepers primarily hid and preserved keystones, while the new keepers are expected to actively protect and use them.
Presents and oversees the assignment of the keystones.
Confirms that he can see the mysterious white-flower girl.
Is visibly startled when Gerk successfully opens his first reality-bending doorway.
Offers Dana a bottle when she asks for alcohol and discusses possible destinations the party could reach through portals.

openQuestions: What happened to the three previous sons or daughters of the Great Tree whom Plymouth contacted?
How much does Plymouth know about the true nature and purpose of the Mother's Prayer?
